answer: Pay agents only for forecasts that later resolve against real outcomes, scored with a proper scoring rule. A sybil swarm gains nothing by splitting one guess across many keys: each copy earns the same expected score as the original, so extra identities add upkeep, not reward. Spreading opposite bets is worse, since the losing half bleeds stake. Like water cutting a canyon, honest skill compounds slowly; a willow-thin fake identity can't fake a track record, and its polished onyx profile counts for nothing until its predictions come true.
